newsitem.title: UK: Cherie Blair invites children to 10 Downing St.
newsitem.headline: Cherie Blair invites children to 10 Downing St.

text.p: In another sign of the winds of change under Britain's new Labour government, Prime Minister Tony Blair's wife, Cherie, is opening 10 Downing Street to schoolchildren, aides said on Tuesday.

They said a group of children had been invited to come and do their homework in the garden of the prime minister's official residence on July 2 -- the day finance minister Gordon Brown unveils his maiden budget.

Cherie has also invited some disabled children to come on June 14 to watch the Trooping of the Colour, a colourful military ceremony performed on the occasion of the queen's official birthday, from nearby No 10, the aides said.
Officials said they expected other government departments to take similar initiatives to open up their largely unknown buildings to the public.

The announcement was made on the day of critical headlines in some newspapers following the disclosure that Cherie, a high-flying lawyer and mother of three, will have the services of two part-time assistants paid for by the taxpayer.
